D6_registry_and_snapshot_custody.stage_a_repair: builtin scalars (int, str, bytes, float, bool) are refused outright with a typed TypeError; a genuine registry object is now PINNED with an owned reference and released on dealloc. Stage A remains NON-AUTHORIZING and cannot decide or require anything.

D7_trusted_seam.stage_a_before: trusted_semantic_hash was stored but NEVER called, making the seam inert; combined with D8 Stage A verified only ref.key/content_hash strings
D7_trusted_seam.stage_a_repair: the pinned callable is now genuinely load-bearing. At admission the trusted semantic hash of each relation's semantic_projection() is sealed (relations without a projection seal nothing and are handled gracefully). On EVERY resolve_exact the projection is re-hashed through the same pinned callable and compared, so a changed payload raises 'native owner custody relation semantic projection drift'. This adds NO positive authority.
D7_trusted_seam.stage_a_evidence: test_d7_stage_a_trusted_semantic_hash_is_actually_invoked asserts the spy callable is called during admission AND again at resolve; test_d8_stage_a_detects_mutated_semantic_payload asserts the drift refusal
D7_trusted_seam.stage_b_position: Stage B's seam was already load-bearing (semantic_hash for the custody hash, relation key, projection re-hash and replay identity; canonicalize for scopes; require_positive_authority for the positive guard). This stage added a read-only trusted_seam accessor so a harness can ASSERT the pinned identities, plus a test that rebinding rawlsing_next.pre553_empirical_objects.semantic_hash after construction does not change the replay identity or custody hash the native owner produces.
D7_trusted_seam.assumed_vs_demonstrated: ASSUMED TRUSTED: the three callables supplied at construction are the accepted pre553 implementations - this is a harness responsibility, not something the native code can prove. DEMONSTRATED: once pinned, their identities cannot be re-bound from Python, no live registry or Python owner is consulted for a positive, and caller data is deep validated and deep copied before any trusted call. TCB note: the substitution of the trusted executable alias ITSELF is deliberately NOT tested as an attacker case, per the commission.

D8_payload_drift.stage_a_repair: covered by the D7 projection re-hash; tested with a mutable stand-in admitted through Stage A's duck-typed admission
D8_payload_drift.stage_b_repair: already present at the HQ245 candidate; re-verified with a mutable stand-in whose ref.key and content_hash are left UNCHANGED while semantic_fields is mutated, and the resolve still refuses with 'semantic hash mismatch'
D8_payload_drift.typed_production_analogue_note: the accepted production SourceUniverseRelation is frozen, so the mutate-after-seal shape cannot be produced with it. A mutable stand-in admitted through the exact-class parameter is the honest analogue, and it is what both tests use. Constructing a forged SourceUniverseRelation with a self-inconsistent content_hash was attempted and abandoned: the production constructor derives required semantic_fields from named parameters, so a caller-supplied semantic_fields dict is rejected.
